summary: Constructs a plane equation from three 3D points (a2, a3, a4) using SSE intrinsics. Computes two edge vectors, their cross product as the plane normal N, normalizes N via a Newton-Raphson reciprocal-square-root refinement using global constants xmmword_5D8C40/50, then computes the plane distance D as a dot product whose sign is flipped with xmmword_5D8C30. Writes the quad (Nx, Ny, Nz, D) to output a1 and returns a1.

operations.description: Load first input point from a2 into v5; form edge vectors v6 = point_a2 - point_a4 and v9 = point_a2 - point_a3 via SSE subtract.
v13 = cross product of the two edge vectors using SSE shuffle/multiply/subtract sequence, producing the plane normal N.
v15 = sum of squared components of N (component-wise square plus horizontal add); v15.x = fsqrt of that sum, giving the normal length.

Newton-Raphson refinement of the reciprocal length: v12.x = xmmword_5D8C50 (normalization scale) * (xmmword_5D8C40 (0.5) - squared_length * (1/length) * (1/length)); then v12 is broadcast across lanes.
v17 = normal N * broadcast refinement scale (normalized normal); *a1 = v17 writes plane normal (Nx, Ny, Nz) to output field this+0x0.
v18 = point_a2 (v8) * normalized normal v17, then horizontal reduce (movehl + shuffle) yielding the plane distance D = dot(point, normal).
Write plane distance: a1->m128_i32[3] = D XOR xmmword_5D8C30 (sign-flip mask), storing the distance component with flipped sign.
